children: The Bank of Korea expects the country's solid economic growth and above-target inflation to persist for a considerable time, reaffirming its tighter monetary policy stance. The BOK says in a policy report that it "will determine the timing and pace of additional base-rate increases while closely monitoring price trends, economic conditions and financial stability." The comments follow two consecutive rate hikes in July and August. It also noted renewed tensions in the Middle East may drive up cost pressures, and chip-led export growth may also spill over into domestic demand and demand-side price pressures. (kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com)
